newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end up on LME gains.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended up across the board on Monday due to gains on the London Metal Exchange last Friday, traders said.
The most actively traded August 1997 contract ended at 23,900 yuan ($2,881) per tonne, rising 100 yuan.
It opened at 23,950 yuan, hitting an intra-day high of 24,000 and a low of 23,850.
May rose 170 to 23,650, June 110 to 23,800, July 100 to 23,900, September 100 to 23,900 and October 70 to 23,800.
Combined volume rose to 71,310 tonnes from 38,980.
Copper opened higher but met strong resistance at the key 24,000 yuan level.
Traders said the LME gains boosted the confidence of Shanghai investors with many believing copper would rise further in the short term.

"Though the contracts met strong resistance at the 24,000 yuan level today, investors were still optimistic about the short-term market trend," one trader said. "Firm physical prices also supported the futures prices."
Physical prices are at around 23,600 yuan per tonne in the Shanghai area.
Most analysts said they expected copper to continue testing 24,000 yuan level in the next few days.
But some traders said long-term market trend was not optimistic despite strong trend in the short term.
"Volume rose sharply with slight rise today indicated many investors were building short positions at high levels," a second trader said.
Current domestic producing cost of producers is below 20,000 yuan level, so producers prefer to sell on futures market at such level, some traders said.
"This is why copper met so strong selling pressure at high levels today," the second trader said.
Aluminium ended up, following copper's trend.
May rose 110 yuan to 15,610, June 200 to 15,950 and July 100 to 16,060.
Combined volume rose to 970 tonnes from 850.
The Shanghai Metal Exchange will suspend trading for four days from Thursday to Sunday on the Labour Day holiday.
